result:
result: Recommend download on first use. Do not bundle rg+fd or fff. fff is an MCP server and a library, not a drop-in rg/fd replacement. The claude.ai paths reject or hold bundled executables, and no source says the exec bit survives.

**Sourced facts**

fff (github.com/dmtrKovalenko/fff, MIT; https://github.com/dmtrKovalenko/fff/blob/main/LICENSE)
- The README calls it "a file search library, not a CLI" and has no rg/fd-style CLI. It exposes a Rust crate, a C library, Node/Bun SDKs and an MCP server (https://github.com/dmtrKovalenko/fff/).
- Its MCP tools are `grep`, `find_files` and `multi_grep` (README, https://github.com/dmtrkovalenko/fff/blob/main/README.md).
  - Regex and literal modes, `paths`/`globs`, context lines, `hidden`, and `find_files` glob/regex modes exist.
  - Results are frecency-ranked and fuzzy, and the index is resident in memory.
- It is not a drop-in rg or fd. There is no `--exec`, no `-l`/`-c`-style CLI flags, and no stdout piping. It would replace the Grep/Glob tool path, not shell calls.
- Latest stable is v0.11.0, 2026-09-21 (https://github.com/dmtrKovalenko/fff/releases/latest). A nightly 0.11.1 exists as a pre-release.
- Assets are bare `fff-mcp-*` binaries with no archive, sizes in MB:

| Platform | Asset | Size |
| --- | --- | --- |
| darwin-arm64 | `fff-mcp-aarch64-apple-darwin` | 7.0 |
| linux-x64 | `fff-mcp-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` (also `-musl`) | 12.7 |
| windows-x64 | `fff-mcp-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.exe` | 13.9 |

- The three total about 33.6 MB.
- Each asset has a `.sha256`. The official `install-mcp.sh` pins the tag and the SHA256 values and downloads musl on Linux (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dmtrKovalenko/fff/main/install-mcp.sh).

ripgrep 15.2.0, 2026-07-15 (https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/releases/latest):

| Platform | Asset | Size |
| --- | --- | --- |
| darwin-arm64 | `ripgrep-15.2.0-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz` | 1.7 MB |
| linux-x64 | `ripgrep-15.2.0-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz` (musl only, no gnu x64 asset) | 2.2 MB |
| windows-x64 | `ripgrep-15.2.0-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip` | 1.7 MB |

fd v10.5.0, 2026-08-26 (https://github.com/sharkdp/fd/releases/, https://aimap.page/en/software/fd/download/). The aimap page mirrors GitHub's published sizes.

| Platform | Asset | Size |
| --- | --- | --- |
| darwin-arm64 | `fd-v10.5.0-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz` | 1.27 MB |
| linux-x64 | `fd-v10.5.0-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz` (musl 1.5 MB) | 1.44 MB |
| windows-x64 | `fd-v10.5.0-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip` | 1.46 MB |

- rg and fd together are about 9.5 MB compressed for the three targets, plus a few MB unpacked.
- Licenses:
  - fff is MIT (sourced, link above).
  - fd is listed as Apache-2.0 (winget page https://wingetgui.com/apps/sharkdp-fd).
  - rg and fd license text was not fetched.

Plugin sync and distribution constraints
- In Claude Code, `bin/` is on the Bash tool PATH (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/components).
- claude.ai and Cowork do not install a plugin with a top-level `bin/` (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/manifest-reference, https://claude.com/docs/plugins/build).
- Organization sync and upload also reject a plugin with `bin/`. The docs say to keep executables in `scripts/` and reference them as `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/<name>` (https://claude.com/docs/plugins/org-sync).
- Size limits:
  - Zip upload: 200 MB, 5,000 files (https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13837433-manage-plugins-for-your-organization, https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/plugins-api).
  - Cowork: 200 MB uncompressed, 5,000 files, and a 512 MB marketplace repository archive (https://claude.com/docs/cowork/guide/plugins).
  - Government card: 10 MB per plugin and 50 MB uncompressed, text only, no binaries (https://claude.com/docs/government/config/plugins-and-connectors).
  - Directory submission: files under 5 MiB, and a compiled executable is held for review (https://claude.com/docs/plugins/pre-submission-checklist).
- The upload API allows no symlinks and requires DEFLATE or STORE compression.
- Plugins copy into `~/.claude/plugins/cache/...`, and claude.ai-synced plugins land in `synced/` (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/loading).
- Persistent downloads belong in `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}`, which survives updates (manifest-reference).

Holyagent build
- `/home/user/holyagent/packages/integrations/claude/build.ts:16` runs `chmod 0o755` only for files flagged `executable`.
- `/home/user/holyagent/packages/integrations/claude/src/generate.ts:190-193` flags only `scripts/holyagent` as executable.
- `dist/` has no `bin/`, so the current plugin is not blocked by the `bin/` rule.
- The marketplace entry sources `./packages/integrations/claude/dist` (`generate.ts:71`). That is a git-based sync, so the exec bit would depend on git mode 100755.

**Inference**
- Exec bit: no fetched doc says whether it survives the cache copy, zip upload or org sync. A `.zip` upload carries whatever mode the archive holds, and the sync path is unspecified. The `chmod` at `build.ts:16` plus git mode 100755 is probably enough for Claude Code. It is unverified for claude.ai, and one empirical test would settle it. Note that `scripts/holyagent` already depends on it.
- Bundling about 34 MB of fff binaries, or about 10 MB of rg+fd, fits the 200 MB cap. It conflicts with the 5 MiB per-file rule and the compiled-executable hold for directory submission. It also fails on the Government path. It would likely force a third-party-binary maintenance and security-review burden on every release.
- Bundling rg+fd would still need a per-platform selector. The three targets would ship as three archives with different extensions. The wrapper would then have to unpack at runtime anyway.
- Downloading on first use avoids all of this. Use a version-pinned URL plus a SHA256 into `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}`, as fff's own installer does, and fall back to PATH `rg`/`fd` when present. The cost is a network and `unzip`/`tar` dependency on first run, and it is likely unavailable in sandboxed Cowork.
- If fff is wanted, add it as an optional MCP server (`.mcp.json` `command` pointing at the downloaded binary) rather than as a replacement for rg/fd. It also adds a trust and dependency decision for the root.

questions: Should the first-use downloader be a new holyagent CLI subcommand? That is a dependency and trust decision for the root. Is empirical testing of exec-bit survival through claude.ai upload and sync wanted?
